metadata.title: The Zane Diagnostic Contract
metadata.note: Every diagnostic a conforming Zane implementation may raise, bound to the constitutional rule it enforces. Prose explaining these entries is in doc/language/VIOLATIONS.md; this file is the contract implementations load. Diagnostic ids are stable forever -- like rule numbers, a retired id is never reused. 1.9 (2026-11-05) renames the language from Zui to Zane: the envelope's language value is zane, and no id, severity, level or binding changed. 1.10 (2026-11-08) adds MENU_LABEL_REPEATS_PARENT, MENU_LANDING_NOT_FIRST and MENU_LABEL_DUPLICATE, bound to Rule 116 as amended at v3.16, with the fields LABEL, TARGET and ENTRIES on NAV_GRAPH (language 1.6): 40 diagnostics.

1.name: Syntax
1.decides: the grammar parses; verbs, kinds and structure are well-formed

2.name: Local semantics
2.decides: everything decidable from a single declaration -- the honest target of a standalone verifier

3.name: Cross-pillar
3.requires: a symbol table of entities, actors, state and elements
3.decides: what the declaration cannot know about the system around it

4.name: Projection
4.decides: what only a painted page reveals; measured today by tools/ui-audit.html

diagnostics.summary: Selection has become execution: SATISFIES holds SELECT and ACT without CONFIRM.
diagnostics.invariant: Selection expresses interest, never commitment.

diagnostics.summary: A reading surface mutates: SATISFIES holds READ and ACT.
diagnostics.invariant: A read surface that silently acts is an intent violation.

diagnostics.summary: An act declares no way back: SATISFIES holds ACT, ALWAYS_REACHABLE lacks UNDO.
diagnostics.invariant: Every act has a reachable undo, or declares why it cannot.

diagnostics.summary: A flow that acts cannot be abandoned: ALWAYS_REACHABLE lacks CANCEL.
diagnostics.invariant: Pause, resume, and exit are always reachable; a trapped flow is unconstitutional.

diagnostics.summary: A multi-step flow has no reachable EXIT.
diagnostics.invariant: Pause, resume, and exit are always reachable; a trapped flow is unconstitutional.

diagnostics.summary: Motion or feedback that reports no state.
A declared element traces to no intent.
diagnostics.invariant: Every UI element must trace to at least one intent.

diagnostics.summary: The system holds state the operator must know, and no surface declares showing it.
diagnostics.invariant: An active filter is visible state.

diagnostics.summary: A consequential act names no actor.
Arriving content reserves no space and shoves the reading when it lands.
diagnostics.note: No fixture: undecidable from a declaration. Measured today by tools/ui-audit.html, which is the enforcement ladder working as designed.

diagnostics.summary: A verb in SATISFIES or ALWAYS_REACHABLE is not one of the 22.
diagnostics.invariant: The grammar is closed: a new medium adds renderings, never verbs.

diagnostics.summary: A .zane declaration kind outside the ten this language defines (WIDGET, USER).
diagnostics.note: Warning, not error: the reference implementation accepts these, and the difference should be visible rather than silent. See doc/language/README.md section 6.

diagnostics.summary: A field key appears more than once in one declaration.
Two declarations share a kind and a name.
An INTENT_FLOW declares no intents.
PERSPECTIVE outside its enumeration.
TONE outside its enumeration.
An INTENT_FLOW reference names no declared flow.
A VIBE suppresses an intent another declaration guarantees as ALWAYS_REACHABLE.
diagnostics.invariant: Vibe-invariant rights never flex.

diagnostics.summary: A VISIBLE_ENTITIES name resolves to no entity in the model.
diagnostics.note: A known gap in the reference implementation: VISIBLE_ENTITIES is parsed and emitted to IR but never resolved. Raised with the reference implementation as decision-document 7.4.

diagnostics.summary: SURFACE_AS names a medium outside the ten this language defines.
diagnostics.note: The medium set is closed for the same reason the verb set is: a coverage matrix over media is only finite and checkable if the media are enumerated. The full enumeration and its capability matrix are data in conformance/media.json.

diagnostics.summary: A declaration satisfies, or promises to keep reachable, an intent the declared medium cannot carry at all.
diagnostics.invariant: A new medium adds renderings, never verbs.
diagnostics.note: Print has no UNDO; a lamp has no READ. Only ABSENT raises -- media.json also records 'degraded' carriage (a parallel act becoming serial, a perception becoming a memory task) as data for tools, because a warning firing on every serial surface would be noise rather than law. Cites Rule 82, which became Perceivable State at constitution v3.9 and is what made 'the declared medium' a legal concept.

diagnostics.summary: A value in SIGNALS is not one of Rule 118's five semantic statuses.
diagnostics.invariant: The colours an interface uses to say something about a record split into exactly two families and no more.
diagnostics.note: Closed for the same reason the verbs and the media are closed: a vocabulary that anyone may extend cannot be checked, and a status palette with more values than an operator can keep apart is what Rule 118 forbids. NOT reconciled with TONE, and deliberately so -- TONE is the register the system speaks in (the MESSAGE stratum), SIGNALS is what a value means about a record (the SIGNAL stratum). Each enumeration refuses the other's words, which is correct for two strata and is why both are documented pointing at each other.

diagnostics.summary: An expression field is declared on a declaration that satisfies no intent.
diagnostics.invariant: Every expression declaration traces to an intent, or it is an error.
diagnostics.note: INTENT_ORPHAN one level down, and the rule that keeps the inversion intact: expression is intent's refinement, never a second language beside it. A declaration saying how something should be PERCEIVED without saying what the operator is DOING has inverted the model this language exists to enforce. SIGNALS is the first expression field; ROLE, MOTION, MESSAGE and TEMPO raise the same diagnostic as their grammars land, which is why this id names the stratum family rather than the field.

diagnostics.summary: Every semantic status a surface declares renders as absence in the medium it declared.
diagnostics.invariant: If the system knows something important, the operator must be able to perceive it -- in the medium the surface declares.
diagnostics.note: Declaring muted on a silent channel is not the defect: silence is the CORRECT rendering of 'waiting, inactive', and a sound announcing inactivity is a contradiction. The defect is narrower and needs both axes -- when EVERY value a surface declares renders as absence, the surface promised a perceptible status and rendered nothing at all. The first check that needs the medium enumeration and the signal vocabulary together, which is what the medium axis was closed for. Stated over 'every declared value renders as absence' rather than over muted by name, so the next channel's data does not require a rewrite. Which values a medium renders as absence is data in signal.json, listed only for channels with a shipped renderer -- a medium absent from that table is UNDECIDED and raises nothing.

diagnostics.summary: A ROLE value is not one of the five promises this language defines.
diagnostics.invariant: A declaration may not name a widget; it may name a promise.
diagnostics.note: The five are inert, navigate, reversible, irreversible and proposal, each extracted from a rule that legislates consequence. Deliberately NOT sourced from Set 13, Widget Selection, whose rules prescribe widgets -- sourcing there would have produced card, button and table, defeating the WIDGET exclusion by spelling. Reasoning in doc/ROLE-DESIGN.md.

diagnostics.summary: ROLE is declared on a kind that is not an INTERACTION.
diagnostics.note: A role is per-control, and INTERACTION is the only declaration meaning 'an act bound to an object' -- a control's referent without being a widget. A role on a SCREEN would claim the whole surface is irreversible, which means nothing. This raises where TONE and PERSPECTIVE stay silent: both are ignored today when they appear on the wrong kind, and a field that does nothing where it sits reads as a declaration that was honoured. That silence is a gap in those two, not a precedent this one follows.

diagnostics.summary: A control promising to change nothing declares that it acts.
diagnostics.invariant: Form follows role, and each widget plays exactly one.
diagnostics.note: inert informs and navigate changes what is shown, never what is true -- Rule 112 lists following a link, opening a panel and switching a vibe as exactly this class. Either one satisfying ACT is a contradiction between the promise and the intent, and it is the declaration-level form of Rule 119's card that behaves like a button.

diagnostics.summary: A reversible control keeps no reachable UNDO.
diagnostics.invariant: Every act has a reachable undo, or declares why it cannot.
diagnostics.note: Rule 79 requires instant one-click undo for destructive actions, and retired Rule 33 into itself under the title 'Undo over Confirm' -- so the principle is in the law's own lineage. reversible is a promise that the change can be taken back; without UNDO in ALWAYS_REACHABLE the declaration has promised something it does not provide. SCOPED AWAY FROM MISSING_UNDO deliberately: that diagnostic already covers 'satisfies ACT and keeps no UNDO' and cites the same rule, so this one fires only where MISSING_UNDO cannot see -- a control promising reversibility without declaring that it acts at all. Two diagnostics for one defect is noise, and the first draft of this check produced exactly that.

diagnostics.summary: An irreversible control declares an UNDO it cannot honour.
diagnostics.note: Rule 79 reserves confirmation for irreversible system-level operations -- purge a database, revoke credentials -- precisely because nothing can take them back. Offering UNDO on one is worse than offering none: the operator acts believing there is a way back. The mirror of ROLE_PROMISE_BROKEN, and the pair is why the vocabulary needed two values rather than one 'destructive'.

diagnostics.summary: A proposal acts without naming the authority that accepted it.
diagnostics.invariant: Intelligence advises; execution decides.
diagnostics.note: Rule 98: a model's output is a proposal and becomes a commit only through an authority the declaration names. Overlaps HIDDEN_AUTHORITY in spirit and not in reach -- that one is level 3 and needs the actor model, this one is level 2 and decidable from the file, because the role has already said the act was advisory.

diagnostics.summary: A surface declares interactions and gives none of them a role.
diagnostics.note: THE COUNTER-CHECK EXPRESSION_ORPHAN DOES NOT COVER, and deliberately a warning: it is REPORTED and never refuses. EXPRESSION_ORPHAN catches expression without intent; this catches the other direction, and it is the failure doc/ROLE-DESIGN.md section 4 predicted and could not see -- a surface with controls and no roles raises nothing, so the stratum passes by silence. It cites no rule because no rule is violated: nothing in the law requires a role today, and a warning that cited one would be claiming otherwise. Requiring a role was ruled NOT YET on 2026-08-19 (stz-principal LEDGER line 38) and this measurement was ruled in its place, because requiring an unproven vocabulary buys a declared role rather than an accurate one -- invisible under-declaration would become invisible mis-declaration, worse because it turns a silent gap into a green check. Fires once per file, span line 0, counted over roles on INTERACTIONs so a misplaced ROLE does not silence it. What it cannot see: an author who declares no INTERACTION at all.

diagnostics.summary: A field is declared on a kind that does not declare it.
diagnostics.note: Ruling D1, 2026-10-31. Each kind declares the fields DECLARATIONS.md lists for it, plus the four every kind carries (SATISFIES, ALWAYS_REACHABLE, SIGNALS, ACTOR). A TONE on a SCREEN or a PERSPECTIVE on a FORM is read by nothing and does nothing, and until this diagnostic the verifier said nothing, so the author believed it was honoured. That silence was the defect, and it is the gap ROLE_MISPLACED named in TONE and PERSPECTIVE when it closed its own. Generalised from ROLE_MISPLACED rather than replacing it: ROLE keeps its own id, because ids are stable forever, and FIELD_MISPLACED leaves ROLE to it so one defect is not reported twice. Only a known field is judged, and only one the verifier would otherwise ignore there: STEPS, INTENT_FLOW, VISIBLE_STATE and VISIBLE_ENTITIES are read on any kind, so they are not silent and are not judged. A name the grammar does not know is UNKNOWN_FIELD. WIDGET and USER are UNSPECIFIED_DECLARATION's and are not judged. The kind list comes from the declaration tables and is mirrored in the Haro declaration haro/zane.stzu, whose court refused this placement before the verifier did.

diagnostics.summary: A field name is not one the grammar defines in the form it is written.
diagnostics.note: Raised by the parser since the verifier shipped and, until contract 1.5, known only to the CLI's own table of structural ids, so the diagnostic FIELD_MISPLACED and VIOLATIONS.md tell authors to expect for an unknown name was in no catalogue. A field is known in ONE form: a list key (SATISFIES, ALWAYS_REACHABLE, VISIBLE_ENTITIES, VISIBLE_STATE, INTENT_FLOWS, STEPS, REPORTS, SUPPRESSES, SIGNALS) written as a bracketed list, or a value key (INTENT_FLOW, PERSPECTIVE, TONE, SURFACE_AS, DENSITY, MOTION, ACTOR, ROLE) written as a scalar. A name outside both sets is this, and so is a known name in the other form -- TONE [neutral] and SATISFIES READ. It is a failure to read the declaration rather than a judgement of it, so no law applies and the bindings are empty, like DUPLICATE_FIELD. FIELD_MISPLACED judges only a field that is known in the form written. SYNTAX_ERROR, UNEXPECTED_CHARACTER and UNTERMINATED_STRING are the other three ids the parser raises that way; they joined the contract at 1.6, so all four structural ids are now catalogued.

diagnostics.summary: The source does not parse as DEFINE <KIND> <name> ( field, ... ).
diagnostics.note: Raised by the parser since the verifier shipped and, until contract 1.6, known only to the CLI's table of structural ids. One id for every way a declaration fails to have its shape: no kind after DEFINE, no name, no opening parenthesis, no field name where one is due, no value for a field, an unexpected value inside a list, an unclosed declaration, and any token outside a declaration. The subject says which. It is a failure to read the declaration, so no law applies and the bindings are empty. The grammar is GRAMMAR.md; this id carries no sentence of it, because splitting it into one id per failure would catalogue the parser's recovery paths and not the language.

diagnostics.summary: The source holds a character the lexer has no token for.
diagnostics.note: Raised by the lexer, one per character, and the character is the subject. The lexer skips it and goes on, so a single stray character does not hide the diagnostics after it. A failure to read the file, not a judgement of a declaration: no law applies and the bindings are empty. Until contract 1.6 known only to the CLI's table of structural ids.

diagnostics.summary: A string is opened and the file ends before it closes.
diagnostics.note: Raised by the lexer at the line the string opened on, and the lexer stops there, since everything after an open quote is inside it. Usually followed by SYNTAX_ERROR for the declaration the string swallowed, and that is expected, not a duplicate: one says why the text ended, the other what the declaration lacks. A failure to read the file, so no law applies and the bindings are empty. Until contract 1.6 known only to the CLI's table of structural ids.

diagnostics.summary: A menu entry's label repeats the label of the entry it sits under.
diagnostics.invariant: A menu names a section at the parent level and the section's landing page as the first child, and no child label repeats its parent's.
diagnostics.note: Language 1.6, law v3.16. The Principal, 2026-11-08, on the Zane site's own menu: it is not logical to read the main title in the main menu and find it again as one of its children. The section and its landing page are two things, so each has one name: the parent level names the section, the first child names the page. Labels compare ignoring ASCII case, the spaces around them and a leading 'The'. Raised at the child's LABEL. A child entry that names no declared NAV_GRAPH is not judged.

diagnostics.summary: A section with children does not list its landing surface first among them.
diagnostics.invariant: A menu names a section at the parent level and the section's landing page as the first child, and no child label repeats its parent's.
diagnostics.note: Language 1.6, law v3.16. A section is a NAV_GRAPH with a TARGET and ENTRIES; its landing surface is the child whose TARGET is the section's own. Raised when no child leads there (the landing page left out of its band, which the Zane site did from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-08) or when the child that does is not the first. A NAV_GRAPH with ENTRIES and no TARGET is a bar, such as a main menu, and has no landing to list. Raised at the section's ENTRIES.

diagnostics.summary: Two entries at one level of a menu share a label.
diagnostics.invariant: No two siblings share a label.
diagnostics.note: Language 1.6, law v3.16. Siblings are the ENTRIES of one NAV_GRAPH. Labels compare ignoring ASCII case, the spaces around them and a leading 'The', so 'Invoices' and 'The invoices' are one name. Raised at the later sibling's LABEL, naming the earlier one.
